titleZh: 双节订单提前进来，酒店该先砍服务，还是先把服务分层？
titleEn: Holiday Bookings Are Arriving Early. Should a Hotel Cut Service First, or Segment It First?
summaryZh: 高峰订单提前到来时，酒店不应整体砍服务或全面增人。用不可失约、可预约、可替代三层服务，加上20笔订单穿行，先守住已售承诺，再决定产能。
summaryEn: Early bookings are a preparation signal, not an instruction to cut or add service everywhere. Segment services into protected promises, smoothable experiences and substitutable convenience, then test the plan through 20 reservations.
contentZh:
双节订单提前进来，酒店该先砍服务，还是先把服务分层？

订单提前进来时，酒店最容易开错的一场会，是怎么把人力再压一压。真正要先解决的不是服务多不多，而是哪些服务一旦失约，会直接损害客人的信任、让现场更忙、最后还要花更多钱补救。市场热度值得酒店提前准备，但它不能自动说明单店该全面增人、全面降配，或把全部服务都保留下来。

先给答案：不要整体砍服务，要先分三层。第一层是不可失约的承诺：已售早餐、接送、儿童或长者协助、团队关键节点、确认房型和延迟退房。这些不是加分项，而是信用底线，必须有责任人和备援。第二层是可预约、可削峰的体验：早餐、餐饮、礼宾、接驳和部分活动，可以通过到店前说明、时段预约、区域分流和清晰指引，移开同一时点的压力。第三层才是可替代的便利：电子指引、合作资源和自助工具可以承担部分工作，但不能替代安全、卫生、准确交付和紧急响应。

为什么只看入住率不够？入住率告诉你卖出了多少房，不告诉你这些房会在什么时候、以怎样的复杂度变成工作。同样是85%的入住率，一家以连住休闲客为主的酒店，可能比较平稳；另一家有大量一晚客、家庭客、会议团和已售权益的酒店，前台、客房和餐饮会同时被挤到临界点。按同一比例加减人，不是精细管理。

高峰前的经营会议应回答四个问题：未来14天哪些到店日、到店时段和离店时段最拥挤？哪些订单含有不可失约的权益或特殊协助？哪些服务能通过预约、分时或前置信息削峰？一旦某个环节失约，谁有权立即调人、外援或补偿？

用20笔订单做一次服务承诺穿行。不必先做复杂系统改造。选择未来14天最有代表性的20笔订单，逐笔看订单承诺、服务触点、时间窗、岗位责任、备援方案和补救边界。它的价值不在于把每位客人做成个案，而在于暴露销售已经卖出、运营却尚未承接的断点。先修交接与优先级，再讨论加人或压人。

业主应先设体验底线和例外预算；总经理要把优先级翻译成早餐高峰支援、净房协调和团队到店安排；部门负责人每天用关键承诺完成率、办理入住等待、净房交付及时率、早餐等位、首24小时投诉和加班时数校准第二天。若只看人工成本率，团队会学会把成本压低，却不一定把服务做稳。

这套方法适合已有订单、权益和部门交接记录的存量酒店。新开业、重大活动或安全风险较高的酒店，应缩短复核周期。今天的第一步很简单：不先开压人力会议，先选20笔已订订单完成一次服务承诺穿行。酒店先把该守住的服务守住，才有资格决定哪里可以更轻、更快、更有效率。

迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
contentEn:
Holiday Bookings Are Arriving Early. Should a Hotel Cut Service First, or Segment It First?

When bookings arrive early, the wrong first meeting is usually about cutting labour. The better question is which services, if missed, would break a promise to the guest and create more operational cost later. An early market signal is a reason to prepare, not proof that every hotel should add staff everywhere or reduce service everywhere.

Do not cut service as a whole; segment it. The first layer is non-negotiable promises: sold breakfast, transfers, assistance for children or older guests, key group-arrival moments, confirmed room features and late check-out. These are commitments that need a named owner and a fallback. The second layer is service that can be booked or smoothed: breakfast, dining, concierge support, transfers and selected activities. Clear pre-arrival information, time slots and sensible flow design can move work away from the same peak hour. The third layer is convenience that can be substituted: digital guidance, partner services and self-service tools. They may reduce workload, but they cannot replace safety, cleanliness, accurate delivery or emergency response.

Occupancy tells a hotel how many rooms it sold. It does not tell the team when work arrives or how complex it will be. Two hotels can both run at 85% occupancy. One may have stable leisure stays; the other may have one-night business guests, families, groups and sold benefits arriving in the same two hours. Staffing them by the same percentage is not precision.

Before a peak period, management should ask four questions: Which arrival and departure windows are genuinely congested? Which reservations contain non-negotiable promises or special assistance? Which services can be time-slotted, redirected or explained in advance? If delivery fails, who can immediately reallocate people, approve outside support or authorise recovery?

Run a 20-reservation promise walk-through. Select 20 representative reservations from the next 14 days. For each one, map the sold promise, service touchpoints, time window, accountable role, fallback and recovery authority. The purpose is not to personalise every reservation. It is to expose the gap between what commercial teams have sold and what operations has actually prepared to deliver. Start with the guest promise, not the headcount.

Owners should define the guest-experience floor and exception budget. General managers should translate that floor into peak-hour priorities and cross-department support. Department heads should recalibrate daily through promise completion, check-in wait, room-release timeliness, breakfast queues, first-24-hour complaints and overtime. This method is most useful for established hotels with usable reservation and handover data. New openings, major-event properties and destinations exposed to weather or safety disruption need shorter review cycles and closer senior oversight.

Before holding a labour-cut meeting, walk 20 booked reservations through the service chain. A hotel can only decide where to be lighter once it knows exactly what it must protect.

MarvelBros C&T
author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
